final_text:
**Claim 522224 (carrier claim): the model gives a low denial probability, and CARC 16 is the only code that loosely fits.**

The denial label in this project is synthetic. It was built from risk rules, so any reason code attached to this claim is illustrative and not a real payer decision.

**Score:** The model gives a denial probability of 0.0769. The validation-set average is 0.1805, so this claim is 0.43 times that average and -10.4 percentage points below it. The model does not flag it as high risk.

**Most plausible code:** CARC 16 is the closest match. The project's reference paraphrases it as "The claim is missing information or has a billing error." Its project rules are provider_outlier and missing_hcpcs. This claim has no HCPCS code (null), and the principal diagnosis is Z604. I can't say what Z604 means, because no tool returned that. The other codes in the reference (11, 18, 181, 197) each need something this claim doesn't show. Code 11 needs a billed procedure to compare with the diagnosis. Codes 181 and 197 also concern the procedure code or prior authorization, and nothing here shows either. Code 18 needs a duplicate claim, and I have no data on duplicates. This is an inference from the project's rule mapping, not something the model outputs.

**How the score relates:** The model weighs the missing HCPCS value slightly toward lower risk (odds change -10%). Its largest downward pushes are:
- CARR_CLM_BLG_NPI_NUM, -20%
- LINE_PLACE_OF_SRVC_CD, -14%
- ORG_NPI_NUM, -11%

None of these three has a project dictionary entry, so I can't describe what they mean. The score therefore doesn't support CARC 16 for this claim. Even the most plausible code sits on a claim the model rates as unlikely to be denied. I ran no policy search, so I make no policy claims.
